title: The two wires carrying one composition instant must agree on one response
untested_rationale: The finding is produced by wireSkewFindings() in audits/checks/b2-llms.mjs, which reads a live HTTP response header beside the body of the SAME response. The pure half IS tested -- compositionWireSkew(snapshot) is exported and exercised by audits/__tests__/b2-llms.test.ts over both agreement and disagreement, both absence cases, and the transport-dark snapshot -- but the rule fires only when a real CloudFront or Cloudflare hop serves a cached body beside fresher metadata, which no pure-function input can construct. rule_class: operational is what the schema requires of a transport condition, and it forbids a cases[] block; the case coverage lives in the unit suite instead.
rationale:
THE PRODUCER CANNOT CAUSE THIS, WHICH IS THE POINT. mantle-LifegamesPortal/src/lambdas/eventbridge/ComposeLlmContent/index.ts:46 computes `composedAt` ONCE, feeds it to assembleInputs at :56 (which reaches the body trailer, `<!-- composed-at: ... -->`) and passes the same value to all three publishArtifact calls at :82, :87 and :88 (which reaches the S3 metadata header, `x-amz-meta-composed-at`). The two wires agree by construction at the write, so a disagreement observed at a reader is NEVER a producer defect -- it is DELIVERY SKEW between the edge's copy of the body and its copy of the metadata.

NOTHING IN THE ESTATE HELD BOTH WIRES FOR ONE RESPONSE. mantle-LifegamesPortal's C1 reads only the header (audits/checks/c1-freshness.mjs:402, preferring it over Last-Modified); this lane read only the body (COMPOSITION_PATTERNS in b2-llms.mjs). Each is internally consistent and neither can see the other disagreeing. fetchSnapshot already fetched the whole response and discarded the header, so the observation costs one headers.get and no extra request.

The header key is a WIRE TOKEN under atlas decision 0105: renaming it is a producer migration, gated in mantle-LifegamesPortal by test/provenance/wire-key-parity.test.ts. A rename that shipped without this lane moving would present here as a permanently absent header, which this rule deliberately does not report -- see expectation.
policy_note: WARN, NOT FAIL, AND DELIBERATELY NOT RATCHETED. CloudFront can legitimately serve a cached body mid-invalidation, so a skew observed inside a normal composition window is expected rather than defective. Atlas decision 0124 recorded exactly this shape on a sibling artifact: 'some feed.json responses carry an older composition stamp over identical valid bytes. Header age can overstate producer age' (decisions/0124-artifact-assurance-implementation.md:332-333). Promoting this id to `fail` requires an observed false-positive rate that does not exist yet -- this rule is what would produce that rate. Until then it prints, it does not move the exit code, and it does not reach the managed-issue reconciler: b2-llms.mjs folds only `severity === 'fail'` catalog findings into catalogFailures. A warn that reds the weekly step would convert an expected edge behaviour into an alert, which is the failure mode the profile relaxations in llms-txt-h2-no-file-list and llms-txt-non-link-list-item were written to avoid.
applicability: One side (origin or site) of one llms artifact, on a response that carries BOTH an `x-amz-meta-composed-at` header and a parseable body composition stamp. A response missing either wire is out of scope: an absent body stamp is already reported by `llms-{side}-composition-time`, and an absent header means the hop did not forward the metadata -- an absent wire is not a disagreeing one, and inventing a finding from it would fire on every Cloudflare Pages Function response that strips `x-amz-meta-*`.
expectation: Date.parse(response.headers['x-amz-meta-composed-at']) equals the instant parsed out of that same response's body by compositionTimestamp(). Emission is PER SIDE PER ARTIFACT: six responses are examined on a full run, so a skew affecting every one of them emits this finding six times. There is no tolerance window -- unlike the coherence arm's maxCompositionSkew, which compares two DIFFERENT responses that may legitimately be refreshed at different moments, this compares two fields of ONE response that the producer stamped from one variable. Equality is the only correct answer, and any inequality is a delivery fact worth naming.
